# Why try to increase sample size?

Remember when we talked about power in lecture. Power is the probability of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis.  

Power increases as sample size increases. That means that as sample size increases, the probability of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis also increases.  

Conceptually, you can think of this as increasing the amount of information (i.e. the number of observations) that you have in your hands to make a decision about the null hypothesis.  

# Why does this matter for interpretation?

```{r}
set.seed(666)

data_frame <- tibble(
  x = rnorm(n = 100, mean = 20, sd = 0.5),
  y = rnorm(n = 100, mean = 20.2, sd = 0.5)
) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = x:y,
               names_to = "group",
               values_to = "value")

data_frame_small <- tibble(
  x = rnorm(n = 20, mean = 20, sd = 0.5),
  y = rnorm(n = 20, mean = 20.2, sd = 0.5)
) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = x:y,
               names_to = "group",
               values_to = "value")

t.test(
  value ~ group,
  data = data_frame,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

t.test(
  value ~ group,
  data = data_frame_small,
  var.equal = TRUE
)
```
